content:
Hey there! 👋 Totally doable, and you don't need to remember whether you had breakfast — just go slow and back everything up before touching anything .

Here's the safe way to do this without clobbering either profile:

    • 1. Find both profile folders first**

- New computer: open Thunderbird → Help → More Troubleshooting Information → "Profile Folder" → Open Folder. Note this path. - Old computer (from the USB copy): look for a path like `.../Thunderbird/Profiles/xxxxxxxx.default-release`. There's also a `profiles.ini` one level up that tells you which folder is the default.

    • 2. Back up BOTH before doing anything** 🔒

Just copy each full profile folder somewhere safe (a separate folder on the USB, or a "backups" folder on the new machine). This is your undo button if something goes sideways.

    • 3. Don't just overwrite the new profile with the old one**

This is the #1 way people mess things up — dragging the old profile folder on top of the new one can wipe out new mail or duplicate everything weirdly. Instead:

- **Close Thunderbird completely** on the new computer. - Create a **brand new empty profile** just for the import (Thunderbird has a Profile Manager for this — run `thunderbird -P` from a terminal/Run box, or Help → Troubleshooting Info → Profile Manager). - Copy the *contents* of the old profile's `Mail` and `ImapMail` folders into the corresponding folders of this new profile. - Also grab `abook.mab` / the address book `.sqlite` files if you want her contacts.

    • 4. Merge, don't just move**

If she wants everything combined into ONE profile (old mail + new mail together), the cleanest tool for this is the **ImportExportTools NG** add-on 🧩 — install it in Thunderbird, then use it to export the old "Local Folders" as .eml/.mbox and import them into the new profile's folders. This avoids conflicts way better than manually copying raw folder files, especially if account setups differ.

    • 5. Once it's imported, verify before deleting anything**

Check that all her folders, message counts, and contacts look right. Only delete the old data (or wipe the USB) after you're 100% sure. 🙌

If you tell me: - Whether she's on IMAP or POP for her main account, and - Whether you want ONE merged profile or just want to recover the old mail into the new setup as extra folders

...I can give you the exact folder-by-folder steps instead of the general version. 💪
